audit_notes: Checks: cavity Reynolds number Re = u*2d/nu = 0.4*0.12/1.6e-5 = 3000 (transitional); cavity h ~ 4-6 W/m2K; NTU = 2*h_c*H/(rho*cp*u*d) = 2*5*10/(1150*0.4*0.06) = 3.6, so the air heats to a large part of the cladding excess by the top; mean fraction 0.5 is fair. Cladding excess temperature alpha*I/(h_o+2h_c+h_r) = 0.3*300/35 = 2.6 K. Model: steady 1D conduction through the wall with a combined convective+radiative cavity boundary; linear, analytical. Baseline (same equation): exposed wall with aged cool paint: cavity_convective_coefficient = 20 (outdoor h_o), cavity_radiative_coefficient = 0, wall_direct_solar_absorptance = 0.32, wall_longwave_loss = 18 W/m2, air_heating_fraction = 0. Simulation coefficient: combined cavity-side coefficient h_c + h_r = 10 W/m2K. Expected gain ~14%. The stack/wind-cap shaping only matters through cavity velocity; at u = 0.1 m/s the fraction rises toward 0.8 and the gain drops to ~11%. Mechanical: standard rainscreen, no issue. Audit passed.
